positions.text: Legal regulation of artificial intelligence: international experience argues prospectively that European AI and robotics standards will support industry development while ensuring human-rights compliance. That assessment qualifies Kaal's warning that strict AI regulation may stifle innovation by presenting standards as potentially development-supporting. The proposition is normative and forward-looking, not an observed industry effect, and it is not limited to legal AI applications.
